newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus board meets on Premiere deal.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus board meets on Premiere deal.

text.p: The board of French pay television firm Canal Plus met on Wednesday to finalise the sale of the company's 37.5 percent stake in German pay TV channel Premiere, a Canal Plus source said on Wednesday.
The deal also includes Canal Plus buying the 45 percent of Italian pay television firm Telepiu owned by Bavarian media moghul Leo Kirch, the source said.
"If there is a signature with Kirch today, the group could announce the accord after 1800 (1600 GMT), but the details will only be announced after the accord has been finalised," the source said.

Analysts questioned by Reuters estimated the value of Canal Plus' Premiere stake at between 1.7 billion and 2.4 billion francs, and Kirch's Telepiu stake at between 1.3 billion and 1.4 billion francs.
Canal Plus would in addition get a cash payment, which the market expects to be around 900 million francs.
The deal, flagged for months, would give Canal Plus 90 percent of Telepiu. Its subsidiary Nethold already owns 45 percent of the Italian company.
Canal Plus would not try to keep the whole 90 percent, but would sell on to Italian investors, keeping a majority for itself, sources have said.
Canal Plus shares continued their recent rise on the imminence of the deal, touching a new high of 1,245 francs on Wednesday morning before dipping slightly, in a stable overall market.
